script.title: Internal Audit vs Statutory Audit
script.caption_hook: Same books, two auditors. Who do they actually work for?

lines.say: Same books, two auditors? Who do they work for?
Statutory audit tells outsiders accounts are true and fair. Internal audit helps management improve the business.
Members appoint at the AGM. The Board appoints the first auditor and casual vacancies. Government companies: the Comptroller and Auditor General.
The Board appoints, under section 138: a chartered or cost accountant, or another professional. Employee or outside firm.
Statutory auditor gives members an opinion. Internal auditor gives the Audit Committee or Board recommendations.
Law and standards fix statutory scope. The Audit Committee or Board sets internal scope, consulting the internal auditor.
So one looks back, one looks ahead?
Not quite. Statutory audit is periodic, on past financial statements. Internal audit is continuous, on operations, controls and risk.
Can statutory auditors rely on internal audit?
Yes, under SA 610, but they keep sole responsibility for the opinion.
S for Shareholders, an opinion. I for Inside, advice.

check_notes: Writer: Corrected per examiner: appointment (s.139 AGM, Board for first auditor and casual vacancies, C&AG for government companies); internal auditor per s.138 (Board appoints; CA, cost accountant or other professional; employee or firm); scope set by Audit Committee or Board per Rule 13, in consultation with internal auditor; looks-back/ahead reframed; SA 610 (Revised) named. Please verify the casual-vacancy shorthand is acceptable (resignation vacancy needs member approval; not mentioned for brevity).

Checker: Line 4 voice and board 'Vacancy: Board': this is too simple. Under s.139(8), the Board fills a casual vacancy within 30 days. If the vacancy arose because the auditor resigned, the company must also approve that appointment at a general meeting within 3 months. In a government company, the CAG fills the casual vacancy within 30 days, not the Board. Correct version: 'Vacancy: Board (resignation: members approve within 3 months; govt company: CAG)'.

Checker: Line 4 voice 'Government companies: the Comptroller and Auditor General': the CAG appoints the auditor, but members fix the remuneration. Make clear that the CAG appoints the first auditor within 60 days and later auditors within 180 days of the start of the financial year (s.139(5) and (7)).

Checker: Line 6: section 138 applies only to the classes of companies set out in Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, not to every company. Add 'for prescribed companies' so students don't think every company must appoint an internal auditor.

Checker: Line 2 and Line 15: calling statutory audit a report to 'outsiders' is loose wording, because the report goes to members/shareholders, who own the company. Suggest 'tells members (and other users)'.
